subject: SLO checkpoint & probe scope for hosted vs incumbent (post-call)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: SLO checkpoint & probe scope for hosted vs incumbent (post-call)

Alex — quick recap and proposed next steps from today's discovery. Thanks for walking through Veridian's production profile; this note captures what we heard and what we need to run a clean hosted vs incumbent comparison for p95/p99 end-to-end latency.

Summary of targets you mentioned on the call:
- Primary SLO targets to validate: p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 600ms (end-to-end, customer-observed)
- Typical concurrency observed: 30-50 concurrent requests during steady peaks; occasional bursts to ~150 for <30s
- Streaming usage: chunked responses enabled for 40% of requests; average chunk interval ~120ms

What Redwood needs to run the probe (ask list):
1) Representative traffic sample (ndjson preferred) with timing/sequence markers and percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests — we listed a requested sample in the call.
2) A baseline window you want us to compare against (dates/time ranges) and the incumbent's monitoring artifacts (p95/p99 reports, percentiles by route).
3) Target acceptance criteria and any hard ceilings (e.g., anything >1s p99 for core user paths flags fail).
4) A 4-hour POC window and a follow-up 2-hour alignment call to review results and first-pass remediation (timing proposal below).

Proposed schedule:
- Mon Nov 23 / Tue Nov 24: ingest Veridian sample + sanity checks (Redwood infra team)
- Wed Nov 25 09:00-13:00 PT: POC probe run (two 60m steady-state runs + short burst tests)
- Thu Nov 26 10:00 PT: result review + next-step sync (30–60m)

Attachments: placeholder SLO probe plan (slo_probe_plan.xlsx) — contains run order, metrics collected, and dashboard links we will populate. Also please attach the traffic sample as ndjson if possible (we suggested veridian_traffic_sample.ndjson).

Immediate asks (can you confirm by EOD Monday):
- Drop the sample ndjson to the Drive link (or reply with file)
- Confirm whether any payloads must remain redacted/PII-stripped for us to run tests
- Confirm the steady-state concurrency number you want us to replicate (30 or 50) and your preferred 4-hour window for the POC

I'll loop in Ben for measurement and scoring details and Marissa for run coordination. If anything above doesn't match what you expect, please call it out.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

--
Attachment stubs: slo_probe_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet: run-order, metrics), veridian_traffic_sample.ndjson (expected, not yet provided)
From: Alex Morgan <alex@veridian.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLO checkpoint & probe scope for hosted vs incumbent (post-call)

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the concise plan. Confirming details and dropping the traffic notes inline:

Current incumbent numbers (what we see instrumented at the edge):
- Measured p95 (end-to-end) for our primary text-gen route: ~120ms
- Measured p99: typically ~700-1,200ms (depends on burst behavior and queueing in the incumbent stack)
- Concurrency: steady peaks are 30–40; we commonly see a 2x–4x spike pattern during morning batch windows; today we plan for a conservative burst sim to 150 QPS
- Streaming: roughly 40% of calls use streaming; streaming chunk sizes average 512–1,024 bytes and the client expects first byte within 100–200ms in normal conditions

Files: attaching a sanitized sample traffic file (veridian_traffic_sample.ndjson) and a short CSV with route-specific p95/p99 snapshots. I dropped both to the Drive link you shared.

Constraints: please do not rehydrate any PHI fields — samples are already masked. Also we need to keep the POC within our business hours window (08:00–18:00 PT) to ensure on-call coverage.

Acceptance guidance: our product PM wants to see p95 parity or improvement vs incumbent and p99 materially improved (we'd expect p99 under 600ms to be competitive). If Redwood can demonstrate p99 reduced consistently across the steady-state runs, we'll consider a technical fit for migration.

We can agree to the schedule you proposed. Confirming Wed Nov 25 09:00-13:00 PT as long as Redwood keeps the burst test to 2 short 30s spikes (we'll monitor).

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Director of Engineering, Veridian Health
alex@veridian.ai

--
Attachments included: veridian_traffic_sample.ndjson (sanitized), veridian_route_snapshot.csv (p95/p99 by route)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 07:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: SLO checkpoint & probe scope for hosted vs incumbent (internal)

Quick internal notes before we run:
- Measurement plan (what we will collect): client-observed end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99), server-side tail (tokenization and final-token times), queue depth, GPU utilization, and stream-first-byte times. Capture per-request trace ids so we can diff identical payloads between incumbent and hosted runs.
- Scoring: compute delta_p95 and delta_p99; also compute %requests where latency exceeds acceptance thresholds (150ms/600ms).
- Traffic shaping: for steady-state runs we'll replay at 30 QPS and 50 QPS (Alex asked for replication of both). For bursts we'll run 2x 30s bursts at 150 QPS with a 5-minute cool-down.
- Observability: set up the temporary dashboard, and make sure the Drive slo_probe_plan.xlsx is updated with exact run tags and time windows.

Questions for the team:
1) Do we want to run quantized model variant for hosted run during the burst to show cost/latency tradeoff, or keep both runs on the same model artifact? I lean toward same artifact to keep apples-to-apples, but we can run an extra variant for ops discussion.
2) Who owns the Figure-of-Merit write-up after the run? I can draft a short executive one-pager if Marissa takes the technical appendix.

I'll slot time 09:00–13:30 PT Wed for the run and be on the call.

-ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 12:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLO checkpoint & probe scope for hosted vs incumbent (post-call)

Alex — thanks for the sample and the acceptance guidance. Confirming final checklist and owners before we start Wed: 

Checklist (owner):
- Traffic sample staged in Drive (Alex / Veridian) — received and validated by Redwood
- SLO probe plan updated with run tags and Drive links (Soojin)
- Measurement dashboard + tracing IDs instrumented (Ben)
- Run coordinator / timekeeper for bursts (Marissa)
- POC result one-pager (Ben draft + Marissa technical appendix)

We will not rehydrate masked fields and will respect your business-hours constraint. We'll run the two steady-state variants (30/50 QPS) as Ben outlined and include the two short burst tests you requested. We'll also do an additional hosted run with quantized weights as an optional third pass — purely informational.

Next step: I will send a calendar invite for Wed Nov 25 09:00–13:30 PT with a short agenda (ingest/checks/run/review). If that slot does not work for anyone on your side, please reply with alternatives.

Looking forward — see you Wed.

Soojin
